usage.outputShape: JSON object at body root (Google Solar API BuildingInsights): body.name, body.center.{latitude,longitude}, body.imageryDate.{year,month,day}, body.postalCode, body.administrativeArea, body.regionCode, body.solarPotential.{maxArrayPanelsCount, maxArrayAreaMeters2, maxSunshineHoursPerYear, carbonOffsetFactorKgPerMwh, wholeRoofStats, roofSegmentStats[], solarPanelConfigs[]}
quirks: Registry 'url' for this endpoint is /api/google-maps/solar/building-insights (Google Solar API) — NOT place-details; the prior existingUsage describing placeId/place-details is for a different route and does not apply here.
Required query params: latitude (number -90..90), longitude (number -180..180), and requiredQuality (enum LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH, default HIGH). All passed as query params, not a body.

requiredQuality controls minimum solar imagery quality; HIGH may 404/empty for locations without high-quality Google Solar coverage — pick a covered urban location (tested Googleplex 37.4450,-122.1390).
Response is very large (~470KB) because solarPotential.solarPanelConfigs[] and roofSegmentStats[] enumerate every panel arrangement; expect heavy payloads.
usage.guide: Call GET https://stableenrich.dev/api/google-maps/solar/building-insights with query params latitude, longitude, and requiredQuality (use HIGH). Pay via x402 ($0.02 USDC on Base). The 200 JSON response is the Google Solar BuildingInsights object at the root: read body.solarPotential.maxArrayPanelsCount and maxSunshineHoursPerYear for solar capacity, body.solarPotential.wholeRoofStats.areaMeters2 for roof area, body.imageryDate for data freshness, and body.center for the matched building location. The payload is large (~470KB) due to per-config panel arrays. Use coordinates of a real building in an area with Google Solar coverage, or it may return no insights.
